title: Enterprise Sales Certification Pathway
summary: A sanitized case study of designing a role-based, region-aware sales enablement pathway that connected curriculum architecture, scenario practice, assessment, LMS behavior, reporting, migration validation, and maintenance.

content.business_need: Create a consistent and maintainable way for internal and channel sellers with different levels of prior knowledge to understand a complex enterprise technology portfolio, recognize suitable opportunities, communicate value, navigate regional requirements, and prepare for the next stage of a sale.
content.audience: Internal sellers and channel partners, from newcomers to experienced practitioners, working with a complex enterprise technology portfolio.
learning_objectives: Recognize customer opportunities that fit the portfolio and identify the most relevant solution path.
Distinguish related solution categories using customer needs, constraints, and business context.
Ask useful discovery questions and connect technical capabilities to customer value without drifting into implementation training.
Recommend appropriate next steps and recognize when a specialist or technical handoff is needed.
Demonstrate required knowledge through objective-aligned assessment and remediation.
content.role: Instructional Designer and Learning Experience Designer. I designed and developed the learning-path architecture and course experience, coordinated review cycles, maintained and updated content, supported LMS configuration, testing and migration validation, and created reporting workflow improvements.
content.design_approach: I treated the certification as a connected learning system rather than a single course. I organized the experience as a progressive journey, separated broadly applicable and regional requirements, layered content for mixed experience levels, tied technical detail to seller decisions, and aligned practice, assessment, LMS behavior, reporting, and maintenance to the same learner outcomes.
content.development_process: I translated approved source material into modular eLearning, multimedia, comparison activities, scenario prompts, knowledge checks, and assessment content. I staged internal QA and SME review, tracked issues and decisions, validated LMS behavior from the learner perspective, and kept released, temporary, and proposed content distinct so updates could be targeted without rebuilding the full pathway.
outcomes: Designed and developed a multi-course sales enablement pathway with role-based content, interactive practice, assessments, review documentation, and LMS implementation support.
The pathway was released and later restructured to provide distinct broadly applicable and regional learning routes.
A supplemental regional assessment and automated spreadsheet workflow provided a practical way to classify regional completion states when platform reporting did not fully match the learning design.
Project records support staged QA, stakeholder review, issue resolution, maintenance, and migration validation without relying on unsupported performance or revenue claims.

detail_sections.title: Turn a broad portfolio into a progressive seller journey.
detail_sections.summary: I organized the pathway so sellers could move from basic context to applied sales decisions. Separating core, regional, and optional requirements kept the main path focused and made future updates easier.

groups.title: Core Path
groups.description: The broadly applicable sequence for the main seller audience.

groups.title: Regional Extension
groups.description: Market-specific learning and assessment stayed separate from the broadly required path.

groups.title: Optional Foundations
groups.description: Deeper technical background remained available without turning sales enablement into implementation training.

detail_sections.note: Recreated architecture using neutral labels rather than internal course, product, or regional names.

detail_sections.title: Serve novices and experienced sellers without designing two separate programs.
detail_sections.summary: The audience ranged from people new to the portfolio to experienced sellers and partners. I used layering and modularity rather than forcing one level of detail on everyone.

items.title: Newer sellers
items.body: Use plain-language scaffolds, predictable sequencing, concise takeaways, and enough context to build a shared mental model before asking for application.

items.title: Experienced sellers
items.body: Provide expandable detail, quick-reference elements, and optional depth so experienced learners can move efficiently without losing access to useful context.

items.title: Role boundary
items.body: Keep technical detail only when it supports a seller decision, customer question, risk discussion, ordering step, or specialist handoff. Route deeper execution content to separate technical learning.

detail_sections.title: Connect seller tasks, practice, assessment, and remediation.
detail_sections.summary: I mapped learning objectives to the decisions sellers needed to make so the assessment checked qualification, comparison, risk recognition, and handoff judgment instead of recall alone.
rows: Identify when a customer opportunity fits the portfolio.
Learner selects the best-fit solution path.
Return to the use-case and customer-need lesson.
Learner matches need, constraint, and solution type.
Recommend the next step and recognize when specialist support is needed.
Learner chooses an appropriate recommendation or escalation path.
Return to positioning and handoff guidance.

detail_sections.title: Use assessment as part of the pathway, not a final attachment.
detail_sections.summary: Formative checks corrected misconceptions during learning, while final assessment and remediation stayed tied to course objectives. A separate regional assessment closed a measurement gap without duplicating the entire path.

items.title: Formative checks
items.body: Use feedback during the course to correct misunderstandings before they reach the final assessment.

items.title: Primary assessment
items.body: Map final items to broadly required objectives and source courses so the certification reflects the learning path rather than isolated trivia.

items.title: Regional assessment
items.body: Keep market-specific requirements in a supplemental assessment rather than forcing irrelevant required learning into the core pathway.

items.title: Remediation
items.body: Point learners back to the relevant topic when an answer reveals a specific misconception or missing requirement.

detail_sections.title: Stage reviews so each reviewer can focus on the right question.
detail_sections.summary: I separated design QA, specialist review, messaging review, assessment review, LMS validation, and post-launch triage so feedback stayed traceable and release decisions were easier to verify.

groups.title: Review workflow
groups.description: A recreated public-safe version of the review path used to move work toward release readiness.

detail_sections.note: Real reviewer names, comments, internal links, dates, and approval records remain private.

detail_sections.title: Treat platform behavior as part of the learner experience.
detail_sections.summary: I supported LMS setup, learner-perspective testing, migration validation, cleanup, and guidance. The goal was to protect valid learner history while finding visibility, mapping, renewal, and reporting issues before they created confusion.

detail_sections.title: Close a platform measurement gap without rebuilding the pathway.
detail_sections.summary: When platform rules could not perfectly enforce and report every regional requirement, I added a supplemental assessment and a lightweight reporting workflow that combined status indicators into a clearer completion decision.

groups.description: Create a clearer status view while keeping exceptions visible for human review.

detail_sections.title: Design the pathway to survive change.
detail_sections.summary: Messaging, naming, features, source ownership, and platform structures changed over time. I used modular boundaries and source tracking so updates could be evaluated and released without treating every change as a full rebuild.

groups.title: Living-content cycle
groups.description: A simple lifecycle for keeping released content separate from temporary or proposed work.

detail_sections.title: Separate what was delivered, observed, intended, and not claimed.
detail_sections.summary: The public case study uses supported qualitative evidence and avoids turning intended outcomes into unsupported performance claims.

items.title: Deliverable
items.body: A multi-course learning path with role-based content, interactive practice, assessments, review documentation, and LMS implementation support.

items.title: Observed outcome
items.body: The pathway was released and later restructured to provide distinct broadly applicable and regional learning routes.

items.title: Process improvement
items.body: A supplemental assessment and automated spreadsheet workflow provided a practical way to classify regional completion states.

items.title: Qualitative evidence
items.body: Project records show staged QA, stakeholder review, issue resolution, maintenance, and migration validation.

items.title: Intended outcome
items.body: The pathway was designed to help sellers recognize suitable opportunities, explain value, distinguish solution categories, and prepare next steps.

items.title: Not claimed
items.body: No public performance gains, revenue impact, customer outcomes, learner counts, ratings, or ROI are claimed without approved evidence.

detail_sections.title: What this project changed in how I design learning systems.
detail_sections.summary: The work reinforced that curriculum design, governance, assessment, reporting, and LMS behavior cannot be treated as separate workstreams when learners experience them as one system.

items.title: What I learned
items.body: A strong learning design has to survive the platform and maintenance realities around it. I also learned to draw a sharper boundary between technical knowledge needed for a seller decision and technical knowledge that belongs in a separate role-based path.

items.title: What I would improve
items.body: I would define routing and reporting rules earlier, establish a source-of-truth inventory before development, prototype certification logic with representative learner profiles, and move more assessment toward fictional performance scenarios.
